Definition: a primary verb (used only in the definite past tense, the others being borrowed from G2046, G4483, and G5346); to speak or say (by word or writing):--answer, bid, bring word, call, command, grant, say (on), speak, tell. Compare G3004.
BiblicalUsage: Épō is the aorist stem of the verb for saying — the 'he said' and 'they said' of the Gospels. It is the form the narrative uses when someone speaks and the story moves on it. You meet it everywhere the Gospels report speech.
TheologicalSignificance: I take épō as it stands — the plain past tense of saying — and let the reported words carry the weight, not the verb itself.
RelatedEvents: The Temptation in the Wilderness; Raising of Lazarus
